final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest escape signal (z=0.964) in a known antigenic (Ca2) site with a positive PLM plausibility score supporting retained replication fitness.
Strong escape (z=0.881) combined with the best PLM score in the pool (z=1.000), suggesting good fitness retention; adds potential glycan-shield escape.
Good escape (z=0.786) in the Sa antigenic region with positive structure compatibility from a prior round, introducing a glycosylation-site-like escape mechanism.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 ranking is stable across escape, PLM, and structure evidence; further evidence is unlikely to alter the final selection.

history.rationale: Position 158 lies in the Sa antigenic site of the H1 head; S158N-type changes are classic antigenic drift mutations that add a potential glycan and disrupt antibody binding while remaining surface-exposed and structurally tolerated.
Sa-site antigenic residue; S158N introduces a potential glycosylation sequon (158-NST) known to shield antibody epitopes while being a naturally occurring H1 variation.
Good escape (0.786) but weak ESM-1v plausibility (0.185); retained as third-best balanced candidate.
Only top candidate with positive structure compatibility (z=0.928) plus good escape (0.786); adds a glycosylation-site-like escape mechanism, raising confidence toward the top two.
Charge reversal at Sa-site residue 157 is a known H1 escape mechanism; the position is surface-exposed on the globular head, so folding/replication cost is expected to be low.
Charge reversal at the Sa antigenic site should disrupt antibody binding; surface-exposed so fitness cost likely moderate.
Highest EVEscape score (0.964) in the pool with moderate sequence plausibility (0.378); best escape-per-plausibility trade-off.
Highest escape z (0.964) with positive PLM (0.378); structure evidence is not applicable (WT mismatch), so it neither confirms nor refutes folding, and PLM serves as the replication proxy.
Residue 159 is a recurrent drift position in the Sa antigenic site; a conservative Ser-to-Thr change alters local epitope chemistry with minimal structural perturbation.
Conservative Ser-to-Thr in the Sa site; changes epitope surface chemistry with minimal structural risk.
Moderate escape (0.619) with very low plausibility (0.014); poor on both axes relative to alternatives.

rejection.reason: Moderate escape (0.619) with very low plausibility (0.014); poor on both axes relative to alternatives.

history.rationale: Position 172 sits in the Ca1 antigenic region; Asp-to-Asn removes a charged epitope contact and can introduce glycosylation context, a common natural escape route.
Antigenic-site Asp to Asn removes a negative charge on a surface loop; conservative size change should preserve folding.
Strong escape (0.881) combined with the maximal plausibility signal (1.0), i.e. escape gain with essentially no predicted fitness cost.
Strong escape (0.881) and the best PLM score in the pool (1.000); structure not applicable, but PLM strongly supports viability.
Residue 187 is in the Sb antigenic site and is historically involved in H1 antigenic drift; Lys-to-Asn neutralizes the positive charge at a key antibody contact.
Sb-site residue; Lys-to-Asn at 187 changes electrostatics of an antigenic loop with modest structural perturbation.
Escape (0.783) is similar to S158N but plausibility (0.018) is far worse; dominated by S158N.

rejection.reason: Escape (0.783) is similar to S158N but plausibility (0.018) is far worse; dominated by S158N.

history.rationale: Conservative acidic swap at Sb-site 188 can subtly remodel epitope electrostatics while being nearly neutral for folding and receptor function.
Very conservative Glu-to-Asp may yield little escape; downgraded pending evidence.
Low escape (0.587) and low plausibility (0.058); dominated.

rejection.reason: Low escape (0.587) and low plausibility (0.058); dominated.

history.rationale: Position 224 is in the Ca2 antigenic site near the receptor-binding pocket; R224K preserves positive charge (fitness-friendly) while altering antibody recognition.
Conservative Arg-to-Lys swap near the Ca antigenic region; low fitness risk but possibly limited escape gain.
Best plausibility among mid candidates (0.510) but lowest escape (0.558); kept as fitness-safe fallback outside Top-3.
Excellent structure (0.972) and PLM (0.510) but escape is the weakest in the pool (0.558); viable but not reward-aligned enough for top-3.
Ca2-site residue 227 is surface exposed; Thr-to-Asn can create a new N-linked glycosylation motif (N-X-S/T) that shields the epitope, a strong escape mechanism.
Surface Thr to Asn could alter local glycosylation potential and epitope recognition in the Ca region.
Escape (0.614) and plausibility (0.075) both weak.
Sa-site 153 is a drift position; Ser-to-Asn modifies local epitope surface with low structural cost, and may support glycan masking depending on motif context.
Sa-site Ser-to-Asn; does not form a glycosylation sequon alone but perturbs epitope surface.
Escape (0.677) below top tier and plausibility (0.023) very low.

rejection.reason: Escape (0.677) below top tier and plausibility (0.023) very low.

history.rationale: Sa-site 154 histidine is surface-exposed; His-to-Gln changes side-chain chemistry and pH-dependent charge, potentially reducing antibody binding with modest fitness impact.
His-to-Gln near the Sa site is plausible but histidine may be structurally involved; downgraded pending evidence.
Good escape (0.824) but very low PLM (0.025) and no structure check; remains a backup, not top-3.
